title: A test run that survives a host restart has its check closed Unknown ("no end before restart") although its launcher keeps running and will write a terminal result
outcome: When a host restart interrupts the turn that launched a still-live test run, the host keeps that run's check open, or otherwise settles it from the run's later terminal result artifact. It does not finalize the check Unknown and advise a rerun while the launcher process is alive. The test-run registry and the check record agree about whether the run is live.
acceptance: Given a durably correlated launcher focused run that is nonterminal at serialize/reload and remains positively live under the existing validated heartbeat/process-identity rules, recovery keeps its associated check pending and reports it as running/pending, with no final restart-only Unknown or rerun advice. The registry and check disposition agree about execution liveness; uncorrelated ordinary runtime-ended checks retain fail-closed recovery.

When that exact run later writes a valid terminal result, recovery/next eligible checkpoint settles the original check exactly once from the matching immutable artifact without an original-runtime completion event or rerun. Pass/fail credit requires all existing owner/request/root/claim-fence/source/fence predicates; missing continuity produces an explicit evidence-gap disposition, never manufactured PASS. Duplicate ticks, checkpoints and another reload cannot duplicate evidence.

Deterministic serialize/reload regressions cover live-to-pass, live-to-fail, PID reuse/stale heartbeat, genuinely gone launcher without terminal output (including terminal-write-versus-exit ordering), malformed/replaced/mismatched terminal artifacts, and source/root/claim/fence changes. Wrong or insufficient identity never attaches another run or earns credit; genuine disappearance resolves with the existing bounded/missing-evidence policy. Full gate plus independent review meet normal landing requirements.
